items.question: How can a wise one come to rest in the yogini heart without relying on further secret talk?
premises: Secret talk has a limited use for one seeking rest.
The yogini heart remains hidden by its own nature.
Resting there allows the wise one to become accomplished.
items.inference: For the wise one, cessation of secret discourse leads to rest in the naturally hidden yogini heart and to accomplishment.
uncertainties: Exact locus of the yogini heart remains context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Enough of secret talk, for the yogini heart is hidden by its own nature. There, the wise one who has come to rest becomes accomplished.

items.question: Through what kind of conduct can one come to see the universe as arising from consciousness relish?
premises: Familiarity arises through conduct of rejecting accepting and disregarding.
Nondual conduct provides a basis for seeing without division.
The relish of consciousness is the source from which the universe appears.
items.inference: One who has grown familiar through nondual conduct sees the universe by virtue of the relish of consciousness.
uncertainties: The balance between rejection and acceptance remains open to practice.
items.plain_english: Having grown familiar with the conduct of rejecting, accepting, and disregarding, one sees the universe through nondual conduct and by the relish of consciousness.

items.question: What must be abandoned before one resorts to the blossomed stage of sound in the sky-formed self?
premises: Prayer born of need and purpose is a form of dependence.
Abandoning such dependence allows rest in the outer and inner self as sky form.
Reaching blissful cessation opens resort to the blossomed stage of sound.
items.inference: Having abandoned need-born prayer, one reaches blissful cessation in the sky-formed self and should resort to the blossomed stage of sound.
uncertainties: The transition between cessation and the sound stage is experiential rather than sequentially fixed.
items.plain_english: Having abandoned prayer born of need and purpose, one reaches blissful cessation in the outer and inner self in sky form and should resort to the blossomed stage of sound.

items.question: How does turning inward at the mouth cause consciousness to bloom into its imperishable lofty wheel?
premises: Turning inward at the mouth is a mode for working with consciousness.
Rightly applied, this causes consciousness to bloom.
That bloom reveals the imperishable lofty wheel of consciousness, non-different from the knowable.
items.inference: By turning inward at the mouth, one rightly causes consciousness to bloom and thence becomes one with the imperishable lofty wheel non-different from the knowable.
uncertainties: The phrase turning inward at the mouth denotes a subtle action rather than a physical gesture.
items.plain_english: Turning inward at the mouth, one should rightly cause consciousness to bloom into the imperishable lofty wheel of consciousness, non-different from the knowable, and thence become that wheel.

items.question: By what means does the knowable dissolve, and where does that dissolution come to rest?
premises: The knowable is dissolved by the fire named consciousness.
Once dissolved, that knowable remains in a dissolved state.
Its final dissolution occurs in the power-fire present in the triangle.
items.inference: The fire of consciousness dissolves the knowable, and that dissolved knowable dissolves fully in the power-fire of the triangle.
uncertainties: The triangle denotes a subtle locus rather than a geometric figure alone.
items.plain_english: That knowable is dissolved by the fire named consciousness. Once dissolved, it dissolves fully in the power-fire present here in the triangle.

items.question: What state does a yogi attain by resting in the seed of withdrawal at that locus?
premises: At that locus, one may rest peacefully in the being of the noble drop of perception.
Resting in the seed of withdrawal is the supporting condition.
Such a yogi attains a state of supreme measure.
items.inference: A yogi who rests in the seed of withdrawal and abides peacefully in the noble drop of perception becomes one of supreme measure.
uncertainties: Supreme measure denotes an experiential limit rather than a quantifiable degree.
items.plain_english: There, the yogi who rests in the seed of withdrawal and abides peacefully in the being of the noble drop of perception becomes one of supreme measure.

items.question: How does the throb of consciousness appear when present in both inner and outer alike?
premises: The throb of consciousness is of the nature of three powers.
It possesses both contraction and expansion.
This holds even in the pair of inner and outer, appearing as beautiful in both common and other forms.
items.inference: The throb of consciousness, possessing contraction and expansion and made of three powers, appears beautiful in common and other forms even within inner and outer.
uncertainties: The distinction between common and other forms is experiential rather than fixed.
items.plain_english: Even in the inner and outer pair, the throb of consciousness, made of three powers and possessing contraction and expansion, appears beautiful in both common and other forms.

items.question: How can outward gaze together with inner aim reach the supreme state when contraction and expansion appear absent?
premises: Even when contraction and expansion appear absent, this arises from the shining forth of that reality.
An inner aim joined with outward gaze is the operative mode.
That mode reaches the supreme state.
items.inference: By virtue of its shining forth, the mode of inner aim with outward gaze reaches the supreme state even when no contraction or expansion is apparent.
uncertainties: The absence of contraction and expansion is an appearance of the state rather than its negation.
items.plain_english: Even when contraction and expansion appear absent, by its shining forth, outward gaze joined with inner aim reaches the supreme state.

items.question: What kind of throb arises thence in the unmeasured freedom of wondrous action?
premises: Thence arises a field of unmeasured freedom with wondrous purpose and action.
In that field arises reflecting, a throb of a distinct kind.
That throb is named eagerness.
items.inference: Thence, in unmeasured freedom marked by wondrous purpose and action, arises the reflecting throb called distinct and named eagerness.
uncertainties: Eagerness denotes a subtle orientation rather than an emotional impulse.
items.plain_english: Thence, in unmeasured freedom of wondrous purpose, act, and form, arises reflecting as the throb called distinct, also named eagerness.

items.question: Why should one come to rest in the mantra circle with regard to that whose vigor is at work?
premises: One should come to rest there in the mantra circle with regard to that whose vigor is active.
Powers beginning with peace arise from identity with that form.
That identity is the reason for such rest.
items.inference: Since powers beginning with peace arise from identity with that form, one should come to rest in the mantra circle in relation to that whose vigor is active.
uncertainties: The specific powers beginning with peace are to be known by experience rather than enumeration here.
items.plain_english: There, one should come to rest in the mantra circle with regard to that whose vigor is active, since powers beginning with peace arise from identity with that form.

items.question: What does the unclosed divine multitude of eyes, named awareness-freedom, bring about?
premises: There is a divine multitude of eyes named awareness-freedom.
That multitude remains unclosed.
By its nature it makes the world self-formed.
items.inference: The unclosed divine multitude of eyes named awareness-freedom brings about the world as self-formed.
uncertainties: The multitude of eyes denotes a subtle capacity rather than a physical set of eyes.
items.plain_english: This divine multitude of eyes, named awareness-freedom, remains unclosed and makes the world self-formed.

items.question: In what state does one stand after all activity has dissolved in the union of great venture?
premises: All activity dissolves in the union of great venture.
One becomes full in the heaped flood of self-rays.
Abiding there, one stands in that state.
items.inference: One whose activities have dissolved in the union of great venture becomes full in the heaped flood of self-rays and stands there.
uncertainties: The great venture denotes a subtle yogic union rather than an outward effort.
items.plain_english: One whose activities have all dissolved in the union of great venture becomes full in the heaped flood of self-rays and stands there.
